object_description: raised pavilion with two introverted classroom levels and numerous interior patios
design_condition: The building follows Cours Roger-Bonvin and occupies the site without residual spaces, raising its ground floor above natural terrain and creating a covered perimeter threshold toward the landscape and city.

positive.statement: The covered outdoor space creates a link between the exterior and interior as a large threshold.
The generous ground floor opens toward the city as a space for communication and exchange.
The two-stage spatiality offers a new way of designing an educational space.
The innovative and daring proposal shakes up thinking about secondary-level learning.
The project’s courage and innovation enabled debate on the college of tomorrow.

negative.statement: The installation occupies the land without leaving residual spaces.
The building reinforces the urban path without completely connecting to it.
The glass-block classroom walls are interesting but not well suited to the use of these spaces.
The corridors leading to the classrooms are undersized for the number of students moving simultaneously.
The spatial proposal seems more suitable for a university-level establishment than a secondary school.
